profile.reading:
Switch Las Vegas 9, also called SUPERNAP 9, sits at 7365 South Lindell Road, Las Vegas, Nevada, on Switch's Core Campus in unincorporated Clark County. Switch held a ribbon-cutting grand opening on August 13, 2015, with press materials giving 470,000 to 471,248 square feet, a minor rounding difference between two Switch releases, and up to 50 MVA of power capacity, with a stated power usage effectiveness around 1.18. SUPERNAP 9 earned Uptime Institute Tier IV Design certification at opening and was expected to add Tier IV Constructed and Tier IV Gold for Operational Sustainability by January 2016, making it, alongside SUPERNAP 8, one of two facilities that made Switch the first carrier-neutral data center company to hold Tier IV Gold ratings at two separate facilities, both genuine third-party Uptime Institute certifications rather than Switch's later self-created "Tier 5" branding introduced in 2017. At the time of the 2015 opening, Switch was already under construction on Las Vegas 10 and Las Vegas 11 together, described as adding roughly 700,000 combined square feet to the Core Campus. Switch's Core Campus overall is marketed today as offering up to 495 megawatts of power upon completion and 100 percent renewable energy, with Switch's Nevada tax-advantages page describing a consumer-use-tax abatement to as low as 2 percent and a 75 percent property-tax abatement on customer equipment, administered through Nevada's Governor's Office of Economic Development. Switch does not name a specific power utility on its Las Vegas pages, though NV Energy is the incumbent utility across Clark County as a matter of public record.

Switch has since built a large solar and battery-storage generation program, including the Switch Station 1 and Switch Station 2 projects and the more recent Gigawatt Nevada development, to support its stated 100 percent renewable energy claim across its Nevada campuses. Clark County's data center cluster, anchored substantially by Switch's Core Campus of which SUPERNAP 9 remains one of the largest and most heavily publicized single buildings, has helped establish Las Vegas as a significant secondary U.S. data center market outside the major coastal and Northern Virginia hubs.

[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This facility, Switch Las Vegas 9, is part of Switch Las Vegas Core Campus in Clark County, Nevada, spanning locations including Las Vegas, Enterprise, and near McCarran. Switch was founded in 2000 by Rob Roy, who serves as CEO and chief engineer, and the company is headquartered in Las Vegas. Wikipedia coverage states that in 2002 Roy acquired a former Enron facility in Las Vegas at auction for 930,000 dollars, strategically located over a fiber optic backbone serving technology companies nationwide, which became the foundation of the Las Vegas Core Campus. That campus has grown to eleven operating data centers spanning over 2 million square feet, with plans to reach 2.3 million square feet across 12 buildings. Switch also operates the Citadel Campus in Storey County in Northern Nevada, a separate 4 billion dollar, 1,000 plus acre development announced in January 2015, and a Grand Rapids, Michigan Pyramid Campus, but those are distinct from this Las Vegas registry cluster. In December 2022 DigitalBridge and IFM Investors completed an 11 billion dollar acquisition, taking Switch private. Data center industry directories place Switch Las Vegas 9 at 7365 S Lindell Rd, Las Vegas, NV. Both datacenterHawk and DataCenterMap independently give this same address. DataCenterMap gives 50 MW for this building, a single aggregator figure, not confirmed by the operator, so not applied to critical_it_mw. Switch own official locations page (fetched directly this session, https://www.switch.com/locations/) names five exascale campuses, the Citadel in Tahoe Reno, the Pyramid Campus in Grand Rapids, the Core Campus in Las Vegas, the Keep Campus in Atlanta, and the Rock Campus in Austin and Houston, but confirms no street address for any campus or building, directing visitors to a contact form instead. This registry rows address, where given below, therefore comes from data center industry aggregator directories, leads-only sources per this projects source hierarchy, not confirmed directly by the operator.

reading.body:
Switch Las Vegas 9 holds 50 megawatts of IT capacity, opened in August 2015 on 471,000 square feet within Switch's Las Vegas Core Campus. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, this translates to roughly 1,250 racks. The facility earned Uptime Institute Tier IV Design certification at opening, qualifying it to host workloads requiring the highest standard of redundancy and availability. Switch has stated a power usage effectiveness of 1.18, placing it in the upper range of efficiency for its era.

The Core Campus, of which Las Vegas 9 is one component, sits in unincorporated Clark County and is marketed as offering up to 495 megawatts total capacity with 100 percent renewable energy. Switch has built solar and battery-storage generation assets including Switch Station 1, Switch Station 2, and the Gigawatt Nevada development to support this claim. The specific power utility serving the campus is not published by the operator, though NV Energy is the incumbent utility across the county.

Las Vegas 9 ranks third among only two facilities in Nevada with published megawatt figures, reflecting the state's limited transparency on data center capacity despite 26 mapped facilities. Clark County's data center cluster, anchored by Switch's Core Campus and tax incentives administered through the Governor's Office of Economic Development, has established Las Vegas as a secondary U.S. data center market. Whether this 50 megawatt building matters to AI scaling depends on its current utilization and the campus's stated expansion to 495 megawatts, neither of which is published in operator specifications.
